The statement highlights stronger recent activity and a tight labor market, but stresses elevated inflation and ongoing policy tightening. The latest Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) suggests credit conditions remain relatively supportive in several areas: domestic banks, on net, eased standards for C&I loans and some consumer credit (e.g., credit cards), reduced costs on credit lines, and reported stronger business credit demand (inventory and accounts receivable financing, plant and equipment investment). Banks also reported stronger demand for HELOCs and auto loans, while CRE standards were largely unchanged and foreign banks tightened C&I standards. Notably, demand for residential real estate loans weakened. Taken together, SLOOS points to still-accommodative credit supply for many borrowers that could cushion activity near term, even as higher rates bite—though housing-related demand is softening and inflation risks remain dominant. Relative to the initial assessment, these SLOOS insights modestly improve the outlook from negative toward neutral.
